target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): add timeouts to model discovery requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock model discovery could wait indefinitely when the Bedrock control-plane model listing calls stalled, leaving setup and model catalog refresh paths without a bounded failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock discovery now wraps both `ListFoundationModels` and paginated `ListInferenceProfiles` SDK calls in a local 30-second abort deadline using the AWS SDK `client.send(..., { abortSignal })` contract. The existing best-effort fallback remains unchanged: profile discovery failures still degrade to no profiles, and failed foundation discovery still returns an empty discovered catalog.

## User Impact

Users and operators get a bounded Bedrock model discovery failure instead of an indefinitely pending setup or catalog refresh when the AWS control plane stalls. Successful discovery behavior and cached catalog behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` passed: 24 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude --model claude-fable-5 --thinking high` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Verified the installed AWS SDK/Smithy client type accepts `client.send(command, options)` and Smithy HTTP handler options include `abortSignal`.

### 2026-07-12 follow-up: exact-head local discovery timeout proof

- Exact PR head verified locally: `29b7aaff4eb2a5396ab4dd875a2b6e2e14935366`.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`.
- Result: passed 1 Vitest shard in 19.32s; 24 tests passed.
- Coverage from the focused file: Bedrock model/profile discovery timeout behavior, abort-aware discovery calls, and fallback completion for stalled discovery paths covered by the PR's local regression tests.
- This is controlled local provider-path proof only. No live AWS Bedrock API call was made, and no real AWS account, region, network stall, or Bedrock control-plane response was exercised.

## Proof

### 2026-07-12 exact-head local discovery tests after latest update-branch

- Exact head tested after normal `gh pr update-branch`: `0600633efef1c0fc30f7b4923066f99d75cd322a`.
- Scope: controlled local Amazon Bedrock discovery regression tests. This is not real AWS Bedrock account/control-plane proof.
- Commands run:

  ```bash
  git fetch fork alix/amazon-bedrock-discovery-timeouts --no-tags
  git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
  git rev-parse HEAD
  git diff --check
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts
  ```

- Result: PASS. `git diff --check` passed; Vitest passed 1 shard, 1 file, 24 tests in 303.42s total wall time. Vitest duration: 7.22s.
- Transcript excerpt:

  ```text
  HEAD is now at 0600633efe Merge branch 'main' into alix/amazon-bedrock-discovery-timeouts
  0600633efef1c0fc30f7b4923066f99d75cd322a
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  24 passed (24)
  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 303.42s
  ```

- Observation: the focused discovery tests cover the local timeout/discovery behavior under controlled test conditions.
- Not tested / remaining review gap: no real AWS Bedrock account, foundation-model discovery, inference-profile discovery, or AWS control-plane stall was exercised. This local proof should not be represented as the real-account proof ClawSweeper requested.
### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled AWS SDK transport proof

- Exact head: `e81f9f99e55ce2c5e29dc8230ab1b10cdd77a252`.
- Scope: controlled local Bedrock control-plane transport proof. This is not a live AWS account or Bedrock service run.
- Command:

  ```bash
  env HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY= no_proxy=     node --trace-exit --import tsx scratchpad/bedrock-discovery-local-proof.mts
  ```

- Harness: a temporary, uncommitted `node:http` server plus the production `discoverBedrockModels()` entry point. The production path dynamically loaded `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock`, created the real `BedrockClient`, and used the AWS SDK's `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK` endpoint override with redacted dummy credentials. The server accepted both control-plane requests and deliberately withheld response headers, then switched to normal JSON responses for a recovery call.
- Redacted transcript:

  ```text
  bedrock-discovery-local-transport-proof
  endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>
  stalled.result.models=0
  stalled.elapsedMs=30270
  stalled.requests=/foundation-models,/inference-profiles
  stalled.closedMs=29972,29972
  recovery.result.models=1
  recovery.model=Local Bedrock Proof Model
  recovery.elapsedMs=25
  ```

- Observed result: the real AWS SDK transport issued both `ListFoundationModels` and `ListInferenceProfiles` requests; a pre-header stall was aborted at the production 30-second budget, both server-side responses observed connection closure, and the existing best-effort path returned an empty catalog. A subsequent discovery call through the same production entry point completed normally and returned one model.
- Not tested: live AWS credentials, IAM behavior, TLS/proxy routing, a real Bedrock region, or an actual AWS control-plane outage. The proof establishes local production-path timeout, socket cleanup, fallback, and recovery only.
